title: Film grade post-FX: vignette, grain, warm/cool split tone, chromatic edge
summary: Full-screen cinematic grade usable on top of any look: contrast, saturation, warm/cool temperature, teal-shadow/amber-highlight split tone, vignette, animated film grain and a slight RGB fringe at the screen edges. Three presets: warm, cool, noir (black and white).
use_when: The prompt asks for cinematic, filmic, gritty, vintage, horror, noir or 'movie-like' visuals, or a first shot needs extra polish.
how_to_use: Instance res://starter/post-film-grade/film_grade.tscn as a child of the main 3D scene. It is a MeshInstance3D full-screen quad (any position, never culled); instance it anywhere in the 3D scene. It draws first in the transparent pass (render_priority -128), so particles and glass drawn after it are not affected. Use only ONE full-screen colour pass (post-film-grade, post-retro, or the grade inside look-cel-anime); post-cel-ink and post-bloom-punch stack with it. UI (CanvasLayer) is not affected. Swap the quad mesh material for grade_cool.tres (night/horror) or grade_noir.tres (black and white). Tune shader_parameter temperature (-1 cool .. 1 warm), vignette (0..1), grain (0..0.3), chromatic (0..0.02), strength (0 = off).
provenance: Made by Summer for the shelf

verified.notes: demo.tscn rendered in Compatibility and Forward+ on macOS (Metal, 1280x720) with no SCRIPT ERROR or shader errors; fresh_test (clean cloud project + preview stage) imports and renders in Compatibility with no errors. Not run in a real browser (WebGL2) or on the cloud's Linux/Mesa GL. Grade, vignette, grain and chromatic edge visible in both renderers. demo.tscn has demo-only lighting nodes (DemoOnlyEnvironment, DemoOnlySun); do not copy those. v1.1 (2026-10-03, owner rule: building blocks only): demo scene and demo scripts moved out; the remaining pieces are unchanged.
